messages:
Priya (CS): Morning team — quick weekly tail-latency snapshot for NimbusCorp onboarding. Focus: p95/p99 by route & model, streaming vs non-streaming. TL;DR: small regressions on streaming chat, one p99 spike on /generate non-streaming.

Marco (SRE): Noted. Summary I pulled from telemetry (last 7d):
```
Route     | Model             | Mode         | p95(ms) | p99(ms)
/generate | redwood-13b       | non-stream   | 420     | 1250  <-- spike Wed 09:13
/chat     | redwood-7b-v2     | streaming    | 210     | 480
/chat     | redwood-7b-v2     | non-stream   | 330     | 760
/embed    | open-embed-2      | non-stream   | 90      | 140
```
Notes: the /generate p99 spike coincides with a retry storm from one customer session (lots of short requests, high concurrency).

Janelle (Eng): Hmm, retries will kill KV cache efficiency. Any payload size or token-length changes for NimbusCorp last week?

Priya (CS): @Alex (Customer) — did you change anything on your side (batching, chunking) during the onboarding tests?

Alex (Customer): We enabled streaming preview on QA for a subset of users on Tue evening. We also increased max tokens for summaries from 300 -> 600 for certain flows. Saw some slowness but thought it was env noise. :grimacing:

Marco (SRE): That explains it — streaming with longer sequences increases per-request compute, and if clients open many concurrent streams it can push evictions. Suggestion: throttle concurrent streams per user and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Janelle (Eng): I pushed a lightweight instrumentation change to trace cache hit rates for streaming flows — deploy-bot just kicked it:
deploy-bot: deployment redwood/telemetry-traces @ 2143658800 succeeded :rocket:

Marco (SRE): After the deploy, I see cache-hit% for /chat streaming rose from ~62% -> ~78% on canary. That cut median throughput tail pressure. Still seeing the /generate p99 outlier tied to the retry loop.

Priya (CS): Action items:
- Alex: roll back the QA streaming preview for the cohort causing retries, or add client-side concurrency limit (owner: Alex) — target: today EOD.
- Janelle: keep the trace on for another 48h and add a small alert if streaming cache-hit falls below 65% (owner: Janelle) — target: +2d.
- Marco: add a temporary routing rule to send /generate requests from NimbusCorp to a lower-concurrency pool until we confirm client changes (owner: Marco) — target: tomorrow morning.

Alex (Customer): Will do rollback today. Also can share request IDs for the retry sessions — do you want them posted here or via ticket?

Janelle (Eng): Post the IDs here (or DM if sensitive). We'll correlate with traces.

Marco (SRE): Quick diag command I used if helpful:
```bash
redwoodctl metrics query --from=2026-03-14T00:00 --to=2026-03-20T23:59 --filter 'customer:NimbusCorp' 
--group-by route,model,mode percentile(p95),percentile(p99)
```

Priya (CS): One more note on spend: overall token spend for NimbusCorp rose ~18% week-over-week due to higher max_tokens and retries. CS flagged renewal risk if cost-normalization isn't addressed. Recommend we include batching/quantization suggestions in next enablement call. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Alex (Customer): Acknowledged. We'll prioritize rollback and then reconvene. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

Priya (CS): Great — I'll update the onboarding playbook with the concurrency guidance and schedule a short enablement session for NimbusCorp next Tue. Next check-in on this thread Friday.

deploy-bot: incident-sla-check: no active incidents; p95/p99 alert thresholds unchanged.

Marco (SRE): Marking follow-ups in ops board.

Janelle (Eng): Adding note to changelog re: streaming cache instrumentation.

Priya (CS): Closing for now; will reopen if new anomalies appear. :eyes:
